brief: JPMorgan's 2027 technical outlook finds a less cohesive cross-asset setup than a year ago. Base metals and AI-hardware equities (semiconductors, SOXL) have broken down, which the bank reads as a leading warning on the manufacturing cycle via its PMI regression model (r-squared 0.52), but the weakness has not yet broadened to other cyclical markets, so the base case stays a continuing mid-to-late-cycle regime. The S&P 500 is expected to hold above 6800-7000 support, with 7000 the critical level into 2027; a sustained break below it would signal a deeper correction toward 6150-6315. DM bond yields keep a bearish medium-term bias behind their 2H26 range breakdowns, but JPMorgan expects range-bound trading rather than the more aggressive yield targets the pure chart patterns imply, with curves staying under flattening pressure. FX and commodities lean more late-cycle: the dollar (DXY, EUR/USD) favors continued strength, AUD/USD is risk-off, and copper, iron ore and gold have all broken key support. The risk: if equity and metals weakness broadens, bonds could whipsaw back into their 2023-2026 ranges.
